sections.title: How this item benefits the environment
sections.html: This item protects trees from damage caused by grazing animals and wild animals.

sections.title: Where you can use this item
sections.html:
You can use this item on trees where you have land under a habitat management, restoration or creation action or option.  

You can also use this item in a Higher Tier Capital Grant with AF1: Plant an agroforestry woodland tree or AF2: Plant an agroforestry fruit tree (with the agreement of the Forestry Commission or Natural England).

You can use this item when planting trees with these capital items:

  • TE1: Planting standard hedgerow tree
  • TE2: Planting standard parkland tree
  • TE3: Planting fruit trees
  • TE4: Supply and plant tree

You cannot use this item with:

  • TE7: Tree guard (large post and rail)
  • TE19: Tree guard (narrow weld mesh)

sections.title: What you must do to use this item
sections.html:
You must:

  • erect tree guards at least 1.5 metres (m) high with posts placed far enough apart that grazing animals cannot reach within 30 centimetres (cm) of the tree stem
  • design the tree guard to allow access for formative pruning, applying mulch and clearing vegetation around the base of each tree

You must construct the tree guards in one of 2 ways.

Option 1

The tree guard must have:

  • at least 3 treated timber corner posts (for a triangular guard) or 4 posts (for a square guard), at least 6cm in diameter and 1.5m above ground
  • top and bottom rails that are 6cm in diameter
  • sheep netting attached between the top and bottom rails
  • a length of barbed wire wrapped spirally around the guard to prevent animals from rubbing against it

Option 2

The tree guard must have:

  • at least 2 treated timber posts, each 6cm in diameter and at least 1.5m above ground
  • 2m of  strong weld mesh  wire wrapped around and securely fastened to the outside of the stakes to form a cylinder (using out-turned spikes if preferred)

You must not:

  • fasten guards to the tree
  • allow guards to constrict, rub or damage the tree in any way

sections.title: Evidence you must keep
sections.html:
You must keep photographs of the completed work and supply them with your claim.

You must also keep and supply on request:

  • any consents or permissions connected with the work
  • receipted invoices or bank statements where a receipted invoice is unavailable
  • photographs of the trees to be protected

Read the record keeping and site visit requirements in the Agreement holder’s guide: Capital Grants, Higher Tier capital grants and Protection and Infrastructure grants for more information.

If you’re applying for this item as part of a Countryside Stewardship Higher Tier (CSHT) application, read the record keeping and site visit requirements in the CSHT agreement holder’s guide.
